title: Choice of a good centre a for two finite measures (5.1, printed (1)–(7))
statement: Choice of a good centre (printed (1)–(7) of the proof of 5.1). Let m, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≥ 1, n := m + 1, d := n + ℓ. There is c = c(m,ℓ) ∈ [0,∞) such that for any two finite Borel measures μ₁, μ₂ on ℝ^d there is a ∈ ℝ^d with Σ_i(a_i − 1/2)² < 1/16 such that, for La := L_{ℓ−1}(a) = {y : ∃ J, |J| = m + 2, y_i − a_i ∈ ℤ ∀ i ∈ J}, every σ ∈ (0, 1/4) and i ∈ {1, 2}: μ_i({x : dist(x, La) < σ}) ≤ c·σ^{m+2}·μ_i(ℝ^d).
lean_statement: ∀ m ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ ℓ → ∃ c : ℝ≥0, ∀ μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ)), IsFiniteMeasure μ₁ → IsFiniteMeasure μ₂ → ∃ a : Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ), ∑ i, (a i - 1 / 2) ^ 2 < 1 / 16 ∧ ∀ La : Set (Eucl (m + 1 + ℓ)), La = {y | ∃ J : Finset (Fin (m + 1 + ℓ)), J.card = m + 2 ∧ ∀ i ∈ J, ∃ k : ℤ, y i - a i = k} → ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ < 1 / 4 → μ₁ {x | infDist x La < σ} ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal (σ ^ (m + 2)) * μ₁ univ ∧ μ₂ {x | infDist x La < σ} ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal (σ ^ (m + 2)) * μ₂ univ
